answer: A farm cannot present clean aliases as the record follows the key, which means laundering reputation through new keys does not work. Histories are stored in summit, checked in river, and lantern makes public each void. Each identity publishes its full failure history, and hiding 13 or more junk verdicts voids its standing entirely when discovered. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 4 times over for the same share of the pool. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
